transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess I'm here because things have been pretty difficult lately. 

Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I've been... I don't know, I've just been snapping at my wife over little things around the house. It's not like me. I'm also putting off jobs and paperwork that I used to stay right on top of without an issue. And I just can't seem to get my head quiet. Even when I go out to the workshop or try to fish to get some peace, my mind just won't settle down.
When your mind won't settle down, are you mostly worrying about a variety of different things in your life, or is it specifically focused on the changes since your father-in-law moved in?

It's pretty much all about him being there, to be honest. I mean, I don't really worry about other stuff. It's just... having him in the house has changed everything. I keep thinking about how crowded it feels, how my routine is messed up, how it's affecting my wife. It all just circles back to him moving in.
In addition to feeling irritable and unable to settle your mind, have you been feeling particularly sad, hopeless, or prone to crying lately?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. And I definitely haven't been crying. It's really just the frustration and the irritability... feeling like I can't relax in my own home. But no, no real sadness or anything like that.
About how long ago did your father-in-law move into your home?
He moved in about five months ago. And, well, this whole thing... the snapping, the putting things off, the racing mind... it all started shortly after that.
Has this situation with your father-in-law caused any significant issues for you at your job or in your social life, beyond just the arguments at home?

Yeah, it definitely has. Work-wise, I actually missed an important filing date for my contractor license recently. I just... I haven't been keeping up the way I used to. I've even had to turn down or delay some small repair jobs because I can't seem to get it together. 

And at home, it's not just the arguments. The whole strain of the situation has put some real tension into my marriage. It's just made it a lot harder for me to follow through on my normal family responsibilities.
Have you noticed any physical changes lately, such as trouble sleeping, muscle tension, or feeling physically tired all the time?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My sleep has been about the same as usual, and I don't feel physically tired or tense. It's really just the mental side of things—feeling irritable and not being able to settle down. But physically, I feel fine.
Do you feel that the level of frustration and the impact this is having on your life is much more intense than what most people would experience in a similar situation?

I don't really know. I mean, I guess anyone would be stressed out having to suddenly live with their father-in-law, right? But... I don't know if most people would be missing deadlines and snapping at their wife like I am. It just feels like it's really getting the better of me, more than it probably should.
